newsitem.title: USA: Northeast says will correct nuke training.
newsitem.headline: Northeast says will correct nuke training.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Friday it will implement corrective actions in its nuclear training programs.
Northeast's three Millstone nuclear plants have been closed for safety violations since March 1996. The utility has said it plans to have all three units ready for restart by early 1998.
Northeast said its subsidiary Northeast Nuclear Energy Company is addressing the deficiences with leadership changes, announced earlier this week, and also with a set of new commitments.
It said in a statement that the commitments were restated in a letter received on Friday from the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).

"We are taking these actions to address identified weaknesses and inconsistencies and to return our training programs to the high standards our employees require and expect," said Jay Thayer, Northeast's recovery officer, Nuclear Engineering and Support Services.
Among other commitments, Northeast has agreed to:
Submit the complete corrective action plan, including a schedule for addressing each of the identified independent review team weaknesses, to the NRC by April 2.
Complete the corrective actions for Millstone units 1 and 3 Licensed Operator Initial Training (LOIT) and Licensed Operator Upgrade Training programs.
Complete corrective actions for the Millstone unit 2 LOIT program.
It will also submit the results of initial reviews of additional classes on all the units to the NRC by March 15.
